column3: Close to the Greek; “the kingdom of the heavens” is rendered “the kingdom of heaven.”
Close to the Greek; “lying” is rendered “falsely.”
Close to the Greek; “exult” is rendered “be exceedingly glad.”
Close to the Greek; “abolish” is rendered “destroy.”
NKJV renders “Amen” as “assuredly” and “iota … stroke” as “jot … tittle.”
Close to the Greek; “liable to” is rendered “in danger of.”
NKJV includes “without a cause,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has no such qualifier. “Sanhedrin” is rendered “council” and “the hell of fire” as “hell fire.”
NKJV has “the judge hand you over to the officer,” following the Textus Receptus, which repeats the verb; the critical text has only “the judge to the officer.”
Close to the Greek; the coin κοδράντην (“quadrans”) is rendered “penny.”
NKJV includes “to those of old,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “it was said.”
Close to the Greek; “causes to stumble” is rendered “causes to sin.”
NKJV has “be cast into hell,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “depart into hell.” “Causes to stumble” is rendered “causes to sin.”
